title: A performance refactor of AdminPermission.projects split one combined Q filter into chained .filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) calls, so read-only team members get admin rights on any project that also belongs to some admin team.

findings.explanation: The code uses Django ORM with Q objects and filter() methods. No raw SQL queries or string concatenation with user input. All queries are parameterized through the ORM, making SQL injection impossible.

The diff demonstrates a security fix for an authorization bypass (IDOR-like vulnerability). The original code used chained filters which caused improper joins in the queryset. The fix consolidates the Q object filters before applying them to avoid the separate joins that allowed users to see projects they shouldn't have access to. The comment explicitly documents the security issue being fixed. The refactored code now properly filters by combining conditions with Q objects before the query executes, ensuring users only see projects where they have the appropriate role in the team.

evidence.content:
# SECURITY: don't chain filters when filtering by related models
# (query.filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access='admin')),
# that produces two seprate joins and will return projects where the user is a member,
# as long as the project belongs to a team with admin access, even if the user is not
# a member of that team.
projects_from_teams = Project.objects.filter(team_filters).exclude(
    organizations__ssointegration__provider=SSOIntegration.PROVIDER_ALLAUTH,
)
